subject: Reranker qualification & eval roadmap — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reranker qualification & eval roadmap — post-demo follow-up

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key outcomes from call:
- Primary goal: improve query-to-document ranking for product search results; current baseline uses BM25 + simple learning-to-rank.
- Candidate retrieval: Findly will supply top-200 candidates per query (embedding-based retrieval).
- Success metrics: your team wants measurable lift on business-focused metrics (click-through -> conversion), but for technical evaluation we'll start with NDCG@10 and MRR@5.

Open technical questions for your engineering team (please reply inline when convenient):
1) How large is your evaluation set? if you can share an initial sample (1k–5k queries) we can bootstrap offline tests.
2) Do you have human relevance labels or click logs we can use for supervised fine-tuning / calibration?
3) Any constraints on latency or token-cost per request for the reranker? (p95 target, budget).

Redwood proposed approach (high level):
- Integration: use Redwood’s /v1/rerank endpoint (server-side) to score candidates. We recommend sending up to 50 candidates per request in the first pass (we can tune).
- Top_k tuning: start with top_k=50 for rerank scoring, evaluate NDCG@10/20; iterate to balance cost/latency.
- Eval plan: Redwood provides an eval harness (script + template) to compute NDCG/MRR, ablation on features (embeddings similarity, recency, metadata).

Attachments: reranker_spec_v1.pdf (integration details + sample payload), findly_eval_template.csv (eval template headers).

Proposed next steps:
- You: share a 1k query sample + labeling policy (if available) — target by Thu, Jun 17.
- We (Redwood): provide a runnable eval harness and example SDK snippet for auth and batching by Wed, Jun 16.
- Schedule 30-min tech pilot to validate integration: propose Tue, Jun 22 or Wed, Jun 23.

If that timeline looks good I’ll open a HubSpot task and drop the calendar invite. Thanks — excited to partner on this.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reranker_spec_v1.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks Marcus — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Eval set: we can export ~2.5k queries with anonymized click logs (will strip PII). We'll attach a small sample by Thursday.
- Labels: we have sparse human labels (~300 queries); most signal is from clicks. Are clicks ok for initial offline NDCG?
- Latency: p95 target for rerank scoring is 180–250 ms; budget we want to keep below $X/token (we'll share exact numbers with procurement).

Questions for Redwood team: 
1) You mentioned sending 50 candidates — does the rerank endpoint accept candidates with precomputed embedding vectors, or do we send only document text? We’d prefer to compute embeddings client-side.
2) For auth: we prefer short-lived tokens tied to our internal identity provider (OIDC) rather than long-lived API keys — is that supported in Private/Dedicated modes?

Looping in Joel (CTO) — Joel, feel free to add any infra/security constraints.

Best,
Sara

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Reranker qualification & eval roadmap — post-demo follow-up

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 09:28 AM Sara Patel <sara.patel@findly.ai> wrote:
> - Eval set: we can export ~2.5k queries with anonymized click logs (will strip PII).
> - Labels: we have sparse human labels (~300 queries); most signal is from clicks.
> - Latency: p95 target for rerank scoring is 180–250 ms; budget we want to keep below $X/token.

Hi all — Karthik (solutions/infra) here. Quick technical answers and recommendations: 

1) Candidate payloads + embeddings: Redwood rerank endpoint accepts both raw text candidates and an optional precomputed embedding per candidate. If you prefer client-side embedding computation, include the embedding vector in the candidates array (floating point list). That avoids duplicate embedding work on our side and reduces CPU work. See example in reranker_spec_v1.pdf.

2) top_k and cost/latency tradeoff:
   - Start with sending top_k_in (candidates) = 50. Redwood will compute rerank scores and return a sorted list and per-candidate score. For offline eval start measuring NDCG@10, NDCG@20, and MRR@5.
   - If p95 latency with 50 candidates exceeds target, try: reduce to 30 candidates, enable quantized model variant (we can recommend q4_0/Z) or use a smaller reranker model for tail traffic.

3) Metrics and statistical testing:
   - Use NDCG@10 as primary; report MRR@5 and recall@k for candidate coverage.
   - For significance: paired t-test on per-query NDCG or bootstrap sampling. For online A/B run at least 2 weeks or until you hit X conversions (we can align on thresholds).

4) Eval harness + labels: clicks are an OK proxy to bootstrap, but click noise biases position. Recommend collecting a stratified human-labeled set (200–500 queries) focused on edge cases (ambiguous queries, new product types). We'll provide an annotation rubric in the eval template.

5) Auth and Private/Dedicated modes:
   - Hosted API: API keys (long-lived) and short-lived OAuth tokens supported via our OAuth flow.
   - Dedicated/Private: we support OIDC integration and short-lived tokens for service accounts; we can exchange tokens from your IdP (SAML/OIDC) to Redwood tokens. We'll document the setup steps.

6) SDK snippet & batching: sample node/python SDK supports sending batch requests with concurrent streaming and automatic KV prefix caching. Quick example (pseudo):
   - python: client.rerank(candidates=[...], model="redwood-reranker-v1", top_k=50, auth_token=...)

7) Structured output / signals: we can return per-candidate JSON with {score, reasons: ["title_match","embedding_sim"]} if you enable the debug flag for offline eval. For production route we recommend turning off verbose reasons to reduce payload size.

Action items (who/when):
- Findly: provide 2.5k sample + click-export by Thu, Jun 17 (Sara + Joel).
- Redwood (Karthik): drop a runnable eval harness (script + Docker) and an annotation rubric by Wed, Jun 16.
- Redwood (Marcus): send calendar invite for 30-min pilot week of Jun 22.

Attachment referenced: findly_eval_template.csv (annotation columns + example rows).

Happy to run a short tech workshop if Joel wants deeper infra walkthrough.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
